1. What I understand: three different questions

The lab has recordings of spikes from selected hippocampal units, aligned to cues and later navigation. A unit is a spike-sorted source treated as a neuron; this is a curated measurement, not access to every neuron or every internal state. We want to relate activity before movement to the path subsequently observed.

The scientific question

Does cue-period activity tell us something about the future path beyond start and goal? If so, is that information organized reproducibly in a low-dimensional way?

The atlas question

What geometry do our already learned representations have, how much does a 3D display hide, and how stable is the relative layout of conditions?

These are related, but not interchangeable. CEBRA is a learned measurement tool, not the hypothesis. Learning a representation, predicting a label, and demonstrating a biological mechanism are three different achievements.

baseline: path ∼ start + goal
neural model: path ∼ start + goal + cue activity

The important comparison is incremental performance on appropriately held-out observations, with nuisance controls and nulls—not whether the second model makes an attractive picture. H1a names that incremental-information component; H1b names reproducible low-dimensional organization of that information. A low-dimensional endpoint code alone is not H1b.

Fact The atlas contains cross-session pseudopopulations—synthetic population rows assembled from multiple real trials. Their valid target is condition-level reproducibility, not one real trial’s complete population state. Judgment This is useful work under recording constraints; it should not wait for an impossible 195-cell simultaneous recording. Its claim must match its construction.

Confidence: high for the inspected code, saved metric definitions and primary-paper methods below. Unchecked here: spike sorting, clock/marker semantics, actual simultaneity, unmeasured gaze/heading/cue confounds and laboratory provenance. We inspected retained artifacts and code, not new raw lab data.

docs/research-questions.md, “H1” and “Data Feasibility Boundary,” defines the question and claim ceiling. docs/analysis-contract.md, “Complementary condition-level contract,” explains what pseudopopulations can support.

2. The whole pipeline: learning happened before the atlas

Behavior labels enter the old pipeline in two places: assembly matches source trials by condition, and Behavior training uses labels to choose positive pairs. In Time training the second use disappears, but the first remains. Therefore “Time has no label in its loss” does not mean “the entire pipeline is behavior-blind.”

scripts/start_goal_cebra_baseline.py:109–190 performs source splitting and label-conditioned assembly. scripts/start_goal_autoresearch.py:409–456 routes those arrays to the historical samplers. scripts/cebra_latent_atlas.py:215–267,354–417 reads the saved representations and attaches labels/support without retraining.

3. The objective and solution method

Objective: audit the saved representation, rather than train a prettier one.

  1. Freeze a shortlist using the earlier study: all three seeds of five endpoint recipe/checkpoint choices and four V9 Time/Behavior/dimension choices.
  2. Add raw-count and PCA8 references for each study and seed: 27 saved CEBRA objects + 12 references = 39 objects.
  3. Verify identities, source splits and shapes. Display training and development with the same coordinates and scale within a run.
  4. Measure geometry in its declared full space and quantify the information lost by the display in a geometric sense—not mutual information or decoding accuracy.
  5. Show original decoder results beside the plots, without fitting or choosing a new decoder.
“No retraining” is precise, not magical. No encoder or decoder was fitted for the atlas. Training-only display PCA was fitted: it is a learned camera, not a new CEBRA model. Historical selection and development-set exposure remain exploratory; freezing this shortlist did not create a pristine test set.

docs/reports/cebra-latent-atlas-protocol-20260924.md freezes the shortlist, transformations and exclusions. scripts/cebra_latent_atlas.py:814–882 checks saved hashes and replays projections/retention; it does not independently recompute every geometry statistic.

4. How it works, from the observation upward

4A. A count vector is not a decoded thought

Suppose a unit has two spikes during a 100 ms cue bin. Its count is 2; its average rate over that exposure would be 20 spikes/second. The historical models here use counts, then training-fitted standardization. A unit with no spikes in an observed bin has count 0. A unit not recorded in that source trial is missing, not silently assigned 0.

The code uses ten nominal 100 ms bins over the first cue second. Counts stop at the actual cue end if earlier; exposure therefore matters. Spike timing within a bin is discarded by this representation. Alignment errors or unequal exposure can change the counts without any change in the animal’s intended computation.

From a vector to a point in neural space

With three co-observed units, a count vector might be x = [2,0,1]. It is already a point in 3D: one axis per unit. With 195 columns it is a point in a 195-coordinate space; inability to draw all coordinates does not mean the vector lacks a precise distance or covariance.

Standardization replaces each cell’s count by (count − training_mean) / training_SD, using pooled training bins. The same means/scales transform development. This prevents high-variance units from dominating merely by scale, but it can amplify low-variance/noisy features. It is a modeling choice, not a biological neutralizer.

4B. Why our population row is synthetic

We repeat that construction with sources belonging to the desired label. Within a session block, the same source supplies every included cell and all ten bins. A second synthetic row can reuse A’s trial 7 but choose a different B trial. That creates another combination, not another recording of trial 7.

Endpoint rows combine 58 session blocks and 195 selected units; V9 rows combine 7 session blocks and 29 units. Same-session grouping preserves what is available together in the source records; it does not itself verify simultaneity. Cross-session noise correlations—trial-to-trial cofluctuations beyond average condition responses—cannot be recovered by assembly.

The deployment catch. The future component label is already used when assembling the V9 population. The encoder’s forward pass uses only neural numbers, but constructing this population for an unknown real trial would require the label used to select sources. This is a conditional representation benchmark, not an operational system for predicting an unknown animal’s next path.

Split source trials before assembly. Otherwise, two apparently different train/development rows can share a real trial’s spikes. This is the neuroscience analogue of placing augmented copies of the same document in both training and test sets. Even source-disjoint trials can share a session, animal, preprocessing assumptions and selection bias.

scripts/place195_v7_v8_neural_experiments.py:151–240 defines count/exposure conventions and missingness. :250–291 preserves complete session blocks during assembly. scripts/cebra_latent_atlas.py:119–191 joins source manifests and reports reuse; this makes the point-count caveat auditable.

4C. CEBRA learns a similarity rule

Contrastive learning trains an encoder by comparing a reference observation to a designated positive and sampled negatives. “Positive” means the sampling rule says these should be related, not “the neuron fired.” “Negative” means a contrast sample, not necessarily a different task class.

Let xᵣ,b be the standardized cell-count vector for synthetic row r at cue bin b. Our historical single-bin network computes a latent vector, z, with E coordinates:

h = MLPθ(xᵣ,b),   z = h / ‖h‖₂MLP: multilayer perceptron, a feed-forward neural network. The normalization makes each latent vector length one.

The selected endpoint network is 195 → 32 → 32 → 16 → 8, with GELU nonlinearities between linear layers and final normalization. V9 substitutes 29 input units and E = 3 or 8. One network call sees one cue bin, not the whole cue or a recurrent history.

Historical recipePositive for an anchor at row r, bin bWhat similarity it encourages
CEBRA-TimeBin b+1 of the same synthetic row, when valid.Nearby cue phases should have related representations.
Ordinary discrete BehaviorA sampled bin with the same endpoint/path class; bin identity need not match.Same-class activity should be related despite other variation.
positive_bin_t03Same ordered start–goal class and same cue bin, potentially another synthetic row.Same condition at the same cue phase should be related.

All three recipes above use global negatives from the training bin pool. A negative can share the class—and the same-bin pool can even select the reference itself as a positive. The separate matched_bin recipe also time-matches negatives; it is not the early positive_bin result in this atlas. No arbitrary adjacency between the end of one synthetic row and the beginning of another is allowed by the Time sampler.

The actual contrastive loss, and an NLP analogy

For normalized vectors, define similarity s(z,z′) = zᵀz′ / τ. The dot product is the cosine of their angle. The paper’s and installed implementation’s criterion can be written:

Lᵢ = −s(zᵢ,zᵢ⁺) + log Σⱼ exp(s(zᵢ,zⱼ⁻))

The first term rewards the sampled positive being similar. The second penalizes the reference being too similar to the sampled negative set. Each reference is compared to every negative in the batch, not only a paired negative. This form uses a separately sampled negative sum, so do not assume the exact positive-in-denominator softmax formula or nonnegative cross-entropy bound familiar from every contrastive library.

In NLP terms: it resembles learning sentence embeddings by pulling together chosen paraphrases and contrasting random sentences. But here the definition of “paraphrase” is the scientific design: adjacent time, matching behavior, or matching condition-plus-phase. A model trained on sentiment labels will often cluster sentiment; the clustering alone does not independently validate sentiment as the hidden cause.

Temperature τ controls how sharply score differences affect the loss. It is not a time duration. Our selected endpoint Time uses τ=1, early same-bin Behavior τ=.3. Thus their difference is not an objective-only controlled comparison.

The Nature paper uses loss as a goodness-of-fit measure under its stated comparisons and derives a batch-size correction. That does not make raw losses across different positive/negative definitions a universal scientific ranking: the objective’s optimum itself depends on those distributions.

At inference, Behavior does not need the label as an extra input to this encoder. Labels selected training pairs; the learned neural-input function then transforms new arrays. Held-out prediction can therefore test reproducible label-associated signal. But memorization, label-conditioned assembly, nuisance correlations and adaptive selection still matter.

Time learning ≠ learning a dynamical model. Our encoder is pointwise. Temporal pairing encourages relations between adjacent bins; it does not estimate a recurrent circuit, a transition law, an attractor’s restoring dynamics, or the animal’s actual movement path.

5. Eight coordinates, eighty features, three display axes

This is the most useful tensor distinction to keep in your head:

Endpoint TRAIN counts as stored:       480 rows × 195 cells × 10 bins
Transpose for binwise encoding:        480 rows × 10 bins × 195 cells
Flatten bins for the shared encoder:   4,800 observations × 195 inputs
Encoder output, E = 8:                 4,800 observations × 8 coordinates
Restore row/bin structure:             480 rows × 10 bins × 8 coordinates

Bin-space plot:        4,800 points, each originally in R⁸
Whole-cue decoder:       480 examples, each with 10 × 8 = 80 features
Whole-cue plot:          480 points, each originally in R⁸⁰

The 83.33% endpoint score belongs to the whole-cue 80-feature decoder. It is not accuracy computed from a single dot’s first three coordinates. Flattening keeps bin order in named feature positions; the historical linear decoder is not an RNN.

Three PCA roles—not one ambiguous “PCA result”

RoleInput → outputWhat is learned / reused?
Feature PCA baselineStandardized cell counts → 8 neural features per bin.A historical pooled-training-bin PCA basis, then ten bins concatenated for decoding. No behavior objective.
Display PCAA chosen representation’s E or 10E coordinates → 3 display coordinates.A new basis fitted to that representation’s training observations and applied unchanged to development.
Spectrum / participation ratioAll coordinates → a summary of variance across linear directions.A descriptive spectrum computed separately for each split; not the development camera used for plotting.

The selected CEBRA runs receive standardized counts directly: the PCA baseline is a parallel branch, not a preprocessing step before these CEBRA encoders. “PCA8/bin” means the same pooled basis is applied to each bin, not ten independently fitted PCAs. Native E=3 CEBRA needs no extra reduction; its bin-space display retains all coordinates by construction.

Projection is a lossy camera

PCA finds orthogonal directions capturing as much centered training variation as possible. Let μ be the training mean and W₃ the first three unit-length principal directions. We display:

u = (z − μ)W₃,   W₃ᵀW₃ = I₃

For 8D embeddings, this discards five linear directions. Rotating the on-screen 3D object changes your view of u; it cannot recover discarded coordinates of z. Recoloring uses different metadata on the same points; it does not retrain or move them.

Axes 1–3 are learned display coordinates, not meters of maze position, individual neurons, or known cognitive variables. The same axes are shared between a run’s training/development panels. Axes across separately fitted runs are not aligned. In the optional fixed-coordinate check, coordinates 1–3 instead mean the first three features of that representation; they are not chosen for separation.

scripts/start_goal_cebra_baseline.py:269–288 fits the pooled feature PCA. scripts/cebra_latent_atlas.py:270–351 reuses those features/reconstructs the V9 reference; :437–466 learns the display basis; :528–600 keeps bin and whole-cue spaces distinct. V9’s older PCA reconstruction is training-recentered using saved float32 directions; it is a geometry reference, not bitwise replay of the old estimator.

6. Five questions about a cloud—and five different answers

A. How complete is the 3D camera?

retained energy = Σᵢ ‖(zᵢ − μtrain)W₃‖² / Σᵢ ‖zᵢ − μtrain‖²

This asks how much squared variation around the training center survives projection. “60% retained” does not mean 60% of path information, 60% accuracy or 60% of the brain. A low-variance direction can carry a highly predictive signal; a high-variance direction can be nuisance.

Development energy includes any mean shift away from the training center. That is why its retention is not identical to summing the top three eigenvalue fractions of a fresh development-centered spectrum.

B. How many linear directions substantially participate?

Let λₖ be covariance eigenvalues—variance along orthogonal directions. Define participation ratio (PR), an effective linear dimension:

PR = (Σₖ λₖ)² / Σₖ λₖ² = 1 / Σₖ pₖ²,   pₖ = λₖ / Σⱼ λⱼ

If one direction carries all variance, PR=1. If four carry equal variance, PR=4. A value like 5.7 says “variance is distributed roughly like several substantially participating axes,” not “there are 5.7 biological factors.” PR can approach 8 for normalized 8-coordinate data even though the unit-sphere constraint leaves at most seven local degrees of freedom.

A first-principles counterexample: one variable, four-dimensional linear spread
z(θ) = (cos θ, sin θ, cos 2θ, sin 2θ) / √2

Only one parameter, θ, is free. Its image is a loop and has intrinsic dimension 1—locally one coordinate describes it. Yet with uniform θ, its four coordinates are uncorrelated with equal variance, so its linear PR is 4. Its vector length is exactly 1. Keeping any three orthogonal principal directions retains 75% of its centered energy.

Ambient dimension is the number of available coordinates (four here). Intrinsic dimension is the number of locally independent parameters (one here). Linear dimension/PR measures spread across straight axes. Topology concerns connectivity and holes. None is a synonym for the others. The atlas measured the first and linear diagnostics, not intrinsic dimension or topology.

C. Does the camera preserve relationships between points?

Distance Spearman correlation checks whether pairs ranked near/far in full space stay ranked near/far in 3D. Top-10 neighbor overlap asks what fraction of each point’s ten nearest eligible neighbors are still neighbors after projection. High global distance correlation need not imply perfect local neighborhoods.

We use a deterministic class-balanced sample of up to 64 synthetic rows (60 for 30 endpoint classes), retaining their bins and excluding within-row comparisons. Cross-row source reuse remains. Tied or duplicate points can make neighbor identities unstable. These are descriptive diagnostics, not thousands of independent statistical tests.

For length-one CEBRA vectors, squared Euclidean distance is 2 − 2 cos(angle). The atlas uses this straight-line chord distance, not distance along the sphere’s surface. Monotonic transformations preserve neighbor ordering in non-tied cases, but are not interchangeable geometric length scales.

D. Does the relative layout of conditions recur?

A centroid is the mean point for a condition. An RDM—representational dissimilarity matrix—records distances between condition centroids. We compare corresponding RDM entries across train/development and seeds. This avoids pretending that “axis 1” means the same thing after a rotated fit.

For bin space we compute condition distances within each cue bin, then concatenate those distance lists; we do not pool between-bin distances. With 30 conditions there are 435 distances per bin, or 4,350 entries across ten bins. These entries are dependent. With V9’s two classes there is just one between-class distance per bin; the atlas deliberately does not report the same multi-condition RDM statistic.

A stable centroid layout can coexist with broad overlapping clouds. It is not exact-trial stability, evidence that source pools are interchangeable, or proof of a particular biological coordinate system.

E. Is the representation useful for the question?

That is a prediction and control question, not answered by A–D. Our displayed decoder metrics are original whole-cue readouts. Endpoint accuracy counts correct 30-way start–goal classifications. V9 uses balanced accuracy, the mean recall of absent and present classes; a constant prediction gives 50% BA. Scores from these two tasks are not a shared leaderboard.

scripts/cebra_latent_atlas.py:420–525 defines spectrum, retention, sampling, fidelity and condition RDMs; :603–627 compares seed RDMs. [4], Dimensionality of Neural Activity and Box 1, supplies the dimension distinctions, not a measured intrinsic dimension for our data.

These path results remain nonpositive under their existing readouts. A low-PR two-lobed cloud does not rescue them. This does not prove absence of path information: the measured inputs, source support, target, representation and readout all limit the test. Nor should one flip predictions after inspecting development labels and call the flipped result confirmation.

1,280 dots ≠ 1,280 independent neural observations. Seed-0 V9 development has 128 synthetic rows × 10 bins, made from 22 distinct source trials and only 29 distinct complete source combinations. Reusing sources changes visual density and weighting without adding independent biology.
Two score/provenance traps worth knowing

The atlas’s original PCA baseline has 82.50% endpoint accuracy with logistic regularization C=1; the later matched C=.01 PCA result was 83.61%. CEBRA endpoint rows in the atlas use that later C=.01 readout. This is not a newly matched decoder comparison, and 82.50% is not a correction of 83.61%.

The earlier review’s roughly 56–66% was the saved training spectrum’s top-three fraction. The atlas’s 56.3–64.2% is development energy under the training camera. They answer related but different questions.

The separate September 24 nonlinear-readout study has its own evaluation objects and report. Its results are not substituted for the historical scores shown here, and the separately completed matched PCA/raw comparison is not part of this atlas.

8. How this compares with the papers

8A. CEBRA’s famous ring is about current position and direction

In Schneider, Lee & Mathis (Nature, 2023), rats ran back and forth along a straight 1.6 m track. The hippocampus dataset had 48–120 putative pyramidal units per rat; spikes were binned at 25 ms. The rat encoder used a ten-sample convolutional receptive field—250 ms of input around each indexed observation. Receptive field means how much input the network can see; time offset separately governs contrastive pairing. Those are different controls even when both have the number ten.

Behavior uses position/direction information to define neural pairs. The continuous time_delta sampler uses empirically observed changes in behavior to choose a nearby context match; it is not identical to pairing adjacent neural bins, and it is not the local discrete same-endpoint sampler. Their colors describe current position and running direction. Ours often describe categorical start/goal conditions during the cue before navigation.

Our pointwise MLP was chosen to avoid crossing trial/cue boundaries. The rat CNN has a richer temporal input window. The fact that both methods are called CEBRA does not make their observation, inductive bias, or target the same. Using a larger window locally would require a separately reviewed boundary-safe design; it is not an automatic improvement.

8B. What the paper measured beyond the picture

QuestionCEBRA rat paperOur saved atlas
What does a point represent?A time-indexed recorded population observation, with a temporal receptive field.A bin of an assembled cross-session population, or an entire synthetic cue.
What labels shape Behavior?Current position/direction, with continuous or mixed context choices.30 discrete ordered endpoint conditions; or a binary future interior-component label for V9 at fixed 4→3 endpoints.
How is prediction tested?Primarily cosine-distance kNN; rat position regression/direction classification, with decoder selection and trial-based nested splits.Existing standardized whole-cue logistic readouts, with source-disjoint development arrays. No new readout fitting.
How is consistency measured?Linear-regression R² between corresponding embeddings; across rats, behavior-binned and normalized mean embeddings.Rank correlation of corresponding condition distances; no fitted axis alignment. Different statistic and invariances.
How is a higher-D representation drawn?Paper states first three latent coordinates in CEBRA embedding figures; the common demo includes native 3D fits.Native E=3, otherwise training-fitted display PCA3; fixed first-coordinate checks also available.
How is topology tested?Persistent cohomology across E=3,8,16,32,64; thresholding with shuffle-trained controls.Not done. Spectra, projection fidelity and condition RDMs are not topology tests.

The paper’s topology analysis used 1,000 sampled points, 10,000 training steps, and 500 shuffled-label-trained embeddings for thresholds. It reported robust loop topology across the tested latent dimensions. These are reported study settings, not a universal minimum sample size or a proposed compute budget for us.

Persistent cohomology, without treating the plot as a proof

Imagine thickening each point into a ball and increasing its radius. At tiny radii the points are disconnected. At intermediate radii they may form a connected structure with an unfilled loop. At very large radii the hole fills. Persistent (co)homology summarizes how long such features survive across scales; a long-lived feature is more interesting than a hole appearing at only one arbitrary distance threshold.

Small distance scaleMany separate pieces
Too little connection
→
Intermediate scaleA loop can persist
Candidate structure
→
Large scaleHoles fill in
Too much connection

Conceptual filtration diagram: it explains persistence across scales, not the exact computational complex, null distribution or a result for our data.

Betti numbers count topological features: β₀ connected components, β₁ independent loops, β₂ two-dimensional cavities. A circle has (1,1,0); a sphere surface (1,0,1); a torus surface (1,2,1). These are topology types, not the number of neural variables, neurons, or freely varying maze coordinates.

A shuffle must address the statistic’s actual construction. For supervised geometry, shuffling only the colors on a fixed embedding does not undo label-shaped training. In our data, relevant label-dependent assembly and selection would also need to be handled, respecting sessions/endpoints/source identity. A random geometric sphere can diagnose normalization, but it is not a complete scientific null for future-path coding.

The normalization trap: length-one vectors in three coordinates lie on a sphere surface. A circular outline in a projection may be a sphere viewed from one angle, not a one-dimensional ring. With E=8, the constraint is a hypersphere in eight coordinates; the 3D shadow is not itself evidence of its topology. The CEBRA paper explicitly contrasts structured embeddings with shuffled embeddings distributed on the constrained sphere.

8C. Evaluation caveat: copy the question, not just the notebook

The Nature Methods section states that rat CEBRA-Time, UMAP and t-SNE were fitted on the full unlabeled dataset, with splitting for the downstream decoder. That is a transductive representation evaluation: the representation sees future evaluation inputs without their labels. This is different from learning all transforms on training sources and then applying them to unseen sources. The paper’s topology calculation also used full-data embeddings. These are method-specific facts, not a claim that every CEBRA experiment in the paper lacked a held-out encoder evaluation.

The current official hippocampus notebook is a demo: it begins with an 80/20 sequential Behavior split, later refits full data for visual comparisons, and includes separate decoding sections. Its hybrid example has three output coordinates; Figure 2’s paper example used five. One shuffle heading says “shuffled neural data,” but the shown code permutes behavior labels. Follow the executed code and the Methods for the specific comparison, not a heading or attractive screenshot.

Our atlas keeps encoders and learned display transforms training-source-fitted, which is appropriate for our transfer question. However, repeated historical development inspection still prevents a new confirmatory claim. Strict transform fitting and pristine scientific evaluation are separate requirements.

8D. The grid-cell torus paper is a different biological experiment

Gardner et al. (Nature, 2022) studied simultaneously recorded entorhinal grid-cell modules. A grid cell fires at multiple locations arranged approximately in a repeating spatial lattice; this is not the same phenomenon as a selected hippocampal unit’s place tuning. Their torus relates to periodic population coordinates in a module, not the physical arena being donut-shaped.

Their visualization took a firing-rate representation through PCA to six dimensions, then UMAP to three. Crucially, the persistent-cohomology analysis used the six-dimensional representation before the UMAP display, with shuffled controls; they also examined preservation across environments/behavioral states. Thus the 3D UMAP picture illustrated the result rather than serving as its sole measurement.

What to borrow: distinguish visualization from quantitative geometry; test stability and relevant nulls; relate coordinates back to behavior.
What not to borrow: an expectation that our cue pseudopopulations should form a ring/torus, a simultaneous-dynamics claim, or proof of recurrent attractor circuitry from a similar shape.

The dimensionality review by Jazayeri & Ostojic (2021) explains why a curved, intrinsically low-dimensional object can occupy many linear dimensions. It supplies the vocabulary and hypotheses—not a license to read biological latent-variable counts directly from our learned PR.

[3] Fig. 1 and “Quantification of toroidal topology.” [4] distinguishes intrinsic and embedding dimensionality. xCEBRA attribution and artificial-agent comparisons are outside this teach unit.

9. A guided reading of the saved atlas

  1. Start at endpoint / positive_bin_t03-step250 / seed 0 / cue-bin vectors. State the point definition aloud before interpreting the shape.
  2. Color by goal, then start, then joint condition. Geometry is fixed. These are categorical labels; similar colors do not establish similar maze locations or paths.
  3. Filter one cue bin. The all-bin cloud pools ten phases. Thin shells or lobes can mix cue-time structure with condition structure. Do not select a striking phase and retrospectively call it preregistered.
  4. Read retention and neighborhood fidelity. Here a 3D display misses substantial structure. Rotating helps see the retained three coordinates, not the other five.
  5. Turn on centroids while retaining the cloud. Means can make a broad distribution look artificially thin. Do not substitute summaries for variability.
  6. Check every seed and the later 3,000-step run. A seed changes optimization and/or source combinations; three seeds are not three new animals.
  7. Compare Time and the PCA reference. Keep temperature and readout differences in view. Do not infer a matched objective effect from this atlas alone.
  8. Switch to whole cue, then to V9 path. Point count and ambient dimension change. V9’s attractive patterns must be read beside nonpositive BA and extremely reused sources.

A displayed line can join bins 0–9 of one synthetic row only. It is a synthetic cue sequence, not the animal moving along a maze path and not a simultaneously observed global neural trajectory.

Transforms do not learn from development.Inspect fit inputs and freeze training mean/basis. Synthetic test changes development drastically and checks the training projection is unchanged.Separate train/development PCA fits can create misleading visual agreement or disagreement.
A zero means observed silence, not missing data.Audit recording masks and exposure, not only finite array values.Missingness/session support may masquerade as neural coding.
Source separation implies the intended generalization level.Check source/session/animal hierarchy and adaptive exposure history.Held-out trials from the same sessions are not a new-animal result; old validation is not a fresh test.
The decoder and target match the scientific claim.Compare endpoint-only prediction to endpoint-plus-neural prediction of the same behavioral outcome, with admissible conditional nulls.Endpoint classification gets mistaken for incremental future-path evidence.
Full-space shape is robust rather than imposed by construction.Check scaling, normalization, sampling, source sensitivity and appropriate full-pipeline nulls before a topology claim.The model or pseudopopulation product construction creates the shape being attributed to biology.

Bad design, plainly Treating this atlas as a matched CEBRA-versus-PCA leaderboard would be bad design because decoder regularization and selected objective temperatures differ. Consequence: an apparent method advantage can be a configuration advantage. Smallest fix for the present artifact: keep the differences visible and do not make that ranking. A new matched experiment can be safely deferred until that comparison is the actual question; none is authorized or run by this lesson.

Bad inference, plainly Treating a supervised pseudopopulation ring as a biological planning attractor would be bad inference because the labels, normalization and assembly can shape it, and simultaneity/dynamics are not established. Consequence: a property of the measurement pipeline is mistaken for a brain mechanism. Smallest fix: label it as learned condition-level geometry and separate each additional claim’s required evidence. There is no safe deferral for correcting the wording.

Reasonable tradeoff: a training-PCA display is simple, deterministic and auditable, but can hide nonlinear structure or low-variance predictive directions. Measuring its limitations is better than silently replacing it with whichever nonlinear projection looks best. Avoiding topology in this pass is a scope decision, not evidence that no topology exists.

Review next—not an automatic new run: first establish what independent-source, endpoint/nuisance-controlled path signal is supported. Then ask whether the corresponding geometry is stable and whether a prespecified topology statistic adds an answer. New controls must preserve real source structure; more pseudorows cannot replace new source evidence. Existing metadata gaps need laboratory verification, not another embedding.

What validation established The completed atlas’s receipts report 125 input hashes, 51 output hashes and 156 forward projection/retention checks, six synthetic tests, and desktop/mobile browser checks. This supports computational integrity within that scope. It does not independently reproduce every geometry statistic, prove the scientific assumptions, or resolve missing biological metadata.

11. Evidence map: what was checked, and what it proves

The parent read the load-bearing code and primary passages. Three read-only branches separately traced the local pipeline, checked CEBRA sources and challenged scientific interpretation. Agreement is not a substitute for evidence or peer review.

Reconciled details—not swept under the rug

  • PCA wording: the actual producers fit one pooled bin basis. Historical “PCA per bin” shorthand must not be read as ten separate bases.
  • Paper versus demo: native dimensions, split stages and hybrid examples differ. The notebook’s shuffle prose also differs from the code; the code shown shuffles behavior labels.
  • Research-branch gaps: one source branch did not recover rat bin width or the full-data Time fitting statement. The parent checked the primary Methods directly: 25 ms bins, ten-sample rat input, and full-data unlabeled Time fitting for the stated rat decoding comparison. “Transductive” is our methodological description, not a claimed verbatim paper term.
  • Consistency ≠ one universal metric: paper regression R² and our centroid-distance rank correlation answer different questions. Linear alignment can stretch geometry; our distances do not fit that alignment.
  • Neighboring studies: the separately completed matched PCA/raw study is indexed in the repository. Its results and the later decoder studies are not substituted for the historical scores in this atlas.
  1. Schneider, Lee & Mathis (2023). Learnable latent embeddings for joint behavioural and neural analysis, Nature. Read Fig. 1–2 and Methods sections “Rat hippocampus dataset,” “Sampling,” “CEBRA models,” “Consistency,” “Decoding analysis,” and “Topological analysis.” These establish the actual rat comparison and controls.
  2. Official CEBRA hippocampus demo. Encoding of space, hippocampus (CA1). Useful for seeing fitting, transform, shuffle and plotting operations; explicitly a demo, not a substitute for the paper’s evaluation protocol. Website interactive example and rat video are presentation references, not our data.
  3. Gardner et al. (2022). Toroidal topology of population activity in grid cells, Nature. Fig. 1 and “Quantification of toroidal topology” distinguish six-dimensional measurement from 3D UMAP visualization.
  4. Jazayeri & Ostojic (2021). Interpreting neural computations by examining intrinsic and embedding dimensionality of neural activity. “Dimensionality of Neural Activity” and Box 1 explain why a curved one-variable representation can have high linear dimensionality.

No external scripts or images are loaded by this lesson. Public links are optional further reading. Local screenshots contain derived private research results: share only through approved channels.

12. Teach-back: critique the claim

A colleague says: “The encoder predicts start–goal classes at 83%, and I can rotate the plot until it looks like a ring—so we have found a low-dimensional future-path plan.”

What is the most important missing comparison, and why would neither a nicer viewing angle nor a high participation ratio supply it?

Answer in your own words. Aim to distinguish the behavioral target, the population construction, and what the geometry measures—not just list cautions.
